title: FAQ:
title_q: “What's the Most Unique Thing About Watsi?”
title_short: Sonam · FAQ 3 · Most unique thing about Watsi
headline: Three things people say make Watsi different: a very small, very human team, a place where you can see your impact, and a very simple way to help.
story: Sonam answers what's the most unique thing about Watsi? with three things she hears from donors all the time. It is warm and a little funny: eight people across seven time zones, and a supporter who asked them to list the whole team.

1. The people. 2. Your own Watsi Impact page. 3. Giving is simple, about 30 seconds, no phone number. She sums up the three, then adds a fourth: the transparency document that lets you follow the money.
do: Open on the question as text over the group walking. Then straight into her answer.
Cut from take 2 only (from 00:33). Keep her three-part order.
Mark each point with one short top text, one at a time.
Show the real impact page and the real donation flow, recorded fresh.
Captions on the whole time she speaks, one line at a time.
dont: Do not use take 1 (00:00 to 00:31) or the flubbed phone-number line (02:03.3 to 02:24.1).
No Smile Train logo or sign in any frame (the pink “Fundación SmileTrain” wall is in Mincho7594).
No child's face without a release. Never name the CSC hospital.
No fake pages. No logo or name at 0:00.
Do not reuse the B-roll ranges used in FAQ 2 (Mincho7629, 7647, 7708, 7713, 7602, 7603, 7632, 7644).

rows.motion: Hook text on frame 1: What's the most unique thing about Watsi? Already on screen at 0:00, does not animate on. Top third, Lato Bold, Watsi yellow #FFCC33, soft shadow, big. It doubles as the thumbnail. Holds to 00:03, then cut straight to Sonam.
rows.sfx: Room tone from the corridor clip, low.
rows.music: Music starts on frame 1. Warm, light, hopeful. No drums, no lyrics.

rows.visual: Sonam to camera, full 16:9 frame: seated, orange T-shirt with a logo, the Clinica Noel name on the wall behind her. Take 2 only (from 00:33): take 1 has a stop at 00:13. Start on “I actually have”.
rows.motion: Hook text off at 00:03. Name super at 00:04 for 3 s, lower left, above the captions, large: <q>Sonam Singh</q> / Director of Marketing & Insights. Captions on from her first word.

voice.quote: I actually have three answers to this one. And they are all things I hear from our community pretty often.

rows.music: Bed 18 to 20 dB under her voice.

rows.visual: Her face on “First, the people”. On “We are spread all over the globe” cut to Mincho7585.MP4 00:06.0 to 00:09.5: women talk in a hallway, one in an orange shirt with a logo (visual.json; it may be Sonam herself, check on scrub). Back to her face on “And somehow people are always like”. Stay on her for the website story: it is her joke.
rows.motion: Top text on her words: <q>First, the people</q>, 2 s. Then number pop <q>8</q> with the line <q>people across seven time zones</q> as she says it, top third, 3 s. Captions on.

voice.quote: First, the people when I talk with donors and partners, they are always surprised when they find out how small our team actually is. We are spread all over the globe, literally eight people across seven time zones, and we are doing a lot. And somehow people are always like, wait, that's the whole team? One time a supporter reached out to say it would be more transparent if we listed our whole team on our website. And we had to get back to them saying, really, that is our whole team.

rows.music: Bed steady. Let “wait, that's the whole team?” land.

rows.visual: Her face on “I think there's something”. On “our medical partners” cut to Mincho7609.MP4 00:28.0 to 00:31.0: healthcare workers in blue scrubs and surgical caps talk in a corridor (visual.json). On “open communication, listening” cut to Mincho7616.MP4 03:20.0 to 03:23.0: women in pink and white talk in a hospital corridor (visual.json). Back to her face on “and actually being there”.

voice.quote: I think there's something really special about being this small and spread out globally. Our technology allows us to scale without having to build a giant organization around it. It's built into our business model. So a lot of our energy can go into the things that really matter, our medical partners, open communication, listening, and actually being there when someone reaches out.

shots.what: Healthcare workers talk in a corridor
Women talk in a hospital corridor

rows.visual: Her face on “Second”. On “You can see everyone you have helped” cut to a screen recording of a real Watsi donor profile (impact page) on a phone: the people helped, the countries, the updates. Record it fresh from a real account Watsi gives us (ask Nick). Never fake a page. Back to her face on “It's all just there.”
rows.motion: Top text on her words: <q>Second, your Watsi Impact page</q>, 2.5 s. Captions on.

voice.quote: Second, your Watsi Impact page. Yes, you have your own Watsi profile too. You can see everyone you have helped, the countries you're giving has reached, and all the updates from the people you have supported, all in one place. And we don't make you ask for this information, which I think is really important to share. It's all just there. You always know your impact and you can actually see it.

rows.sfx: One soft UI tap on the cut to the screen recording.

shots.screen: real Watsi donor profile on a phone, recorded fresh

rows.visual: Her face on “And third”. On “making a donation” cut to a screen recording of the real watsi.org donation flow on a phone, start to finish, sped up to fit. Record it fresh. Back to her face on “We don't ask for your company name.” Cut out 02:03.3 to 02:24.1: she flubs the phone-number line and starts again.
rows.motion: Top text on her words: <q>And third, we make it really simple to help.</q>, 2.5 s. Then number pop <q>30</q> with the line <q>seconds</q> when she says about 30 seconds, top third, 2.5 s. Captions on.

voice.quote: And third, we make it really simple to help. I have watched someone from landing on Watsi who were making a donation in about 30 seconds. We don't ask for your company name. We don't ask for your address.

rows.sfx: One soft UI tap on the cut to the screen recording.

shots.screen: real watsi.org donation flow on a phone, recorded fresh

rows.visual: Her face, from the clean retake at 02:24.2 (“We don't ask for your phone number”). On “Giving should be simple and we think even joyful” cut to Mincho7685.MP4 00:14.0 to 00:17.0: a woman shows how to make a bracelet at the art activity, a child watches (visual.json). Children: use only with a release (ask Nick).

voice.quote: We don't ask for your phone number, which as a marketer makes my life slightly difficult to be honest, but I also think that's the point. You came here to help. Why should you have to spend five minutes filling out a form before you can just do that? Giving should be simple and we think even joyful.

shots.what: Bracelet making at the art activity

rows.visual: Her face on “So those are my three things.” Then the full-frame list card for the three points. Back to her face for the last words if the card ends early.
rows.motion: List card, full frame, from her words A very small: heading <q>my three things</q>, then <q>a very human team</q>, <q>see your impact</q>, <q>a very simple way to help</q>, one at a time on her words. Light cyan background, navy text. Captions stay on over it.

voice.quote: So those are my three things. A very small, very human team, a place where you can actually see your impact and a very simple way to help.

rows.visual: Her face. She adds a fourth point: the transparency document. Stay on her. Hold 0.7 s after “right now.”, then cut to the end card.

voice.quote: And I have a fourth one to wait, our transparency document. It's a little old school. It's just a simple Google sheet, but it makes it easy to follow the money. And while we have done this since day one, we think this level of transparency is only getting more and more important right now.

rows.visual: Clean end card, full frame. Light cyan #D3EDFA background. Navy is never a background.
rows.motion: watsi.org, all lowercase, Lato, navy #2E2844. One line. Nothing under it. No logo before this card.
rows.music: Music out with a 1 s fade.
